arxiv-2506-19666.title: Fast Flexible LSQR with a Hybrid Variant for Efficient Large-Scale Regularization Thanks: The work of the authors was partially supported by the Charles University, project GAUK 376121, and partially by the grant SVV-2023-260711.
arxiv-2506-19666.creator: Eva Mikušová, Iveta Hnětynková
arxiv-2506-19666.description: Abstract . A wide range of applications necessitates solving large-scale ill-posed problems contaminated by noise. Krylov subspace regularization methods are particularly advantageous in this context, as they rely solely on matrix-vector multiplication. Among the most widely used techniques are LSQR and CGLS, both of which can be extended with flexible preconditioning to enforce solution properties such as nonnegativity or sparsity.

arxiv-2510-18358.title: Ensembling Pruned Attention Heads For Uncertainty-Aware Efficient Transformers
arxiv-2510-18358.creator: Firas Gabetni, Giuseppe Curci, Andrea Pilzer, Subhankar Roy, Elisa Ricci, Gianni Franchi
arxiv-2510-18358.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Firas Gabetni, Giuseppe Curci, Andrea Pilzer, Subhankar Roy, Elisa Ricci, Gianni Franchi. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) is essential for deploying deep neural networks in safety-critical settings. Although methods like Deep Ensembles achieve strong UQ performance, their high computational and memory costs hinder scalability to large models. We introduce Hydra Ensembles , an efficient transformer-based ensemble that prunes attention heads to create diverse members and merges them via a new multi-head attention with grouped fully-connected layers.

arxiv-2512-24108.title: Dynamical probing of superfluidity and shear rigidity in different phases of a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate
arxiv-2512-24108.creator: Soumyadeep Halder, Hari Sadhan Ghosh, Axel Pelster, B. Prasanna Venkatesh
arxiv-2512-24108.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Soumyadeep Halder, Hari Sadhan Ghosh, Axel Pelster, B. Prasanna Venkatesh. We show that a sudden change in the polarization direction of the magnetic dipole moments of the atoms in a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) can serve as a useful probe to sense its superfluid and solid-like properties. We find that for small angular deviation of the polarization direction, actuated for instance by modifying an external magnetic field, the superfluid state undergoes an undamped scissors mode oscillation, a characteristic signature of superfluidity.

pmc-11426428.title: A randomized controlled study of auricular point acupressure to manage chemotherapy-induced neuropathy: Study protocol
pmc-11426428.creator: Nada Lukkahatai, Michael V. Nguyen, Jingyu Zhang, Yu-Min Cho, Chitchanok Benjasirisan, Heijingzi Monica Jia, Claudia M. Campbell, Jennifer Kawi, Hulin Wu, Hongyu Wang, Rupsikha Bora, Johannes Thrul, Constance M. Johnson, Thomas J. Smith
pmc-11426428.description: ObjectiveChemotherapy-induced neuropathy (CIN) significantly impacts cancer patients, leading to functional disability, diminished quality of life, and increased healthcare costs amid the ongoing opioid crisis. pmc-12596782.description: Background: Cerebral proliferative angiopathy (CPA) is a rare vascular disorder characterized by diffuse vascular networks intermingled with functional brain tissue, lacking a well-defined nidus. Unlike classical arteriovenous malformations, CPA often involves bilateral arterial supply, fragile neovessels, and hemodynamic instability, posing significant therapeutic challenges.

pmc-12698631.title: Voices from the field: healthcare professionals’ insights on sustaining telemedicine for diabetes management in Hong Kong primary care

pmc-12698631.description: IntroductionDiabetes mellitus is a prevalent chronic illness that imposes substantial health and financial burdens. pmc-13077662.title: The Impact of Chemical Toxicants and Air Pollutants on Neurodegenerative Disorders and Their Underlying Potential Mechanisms: A Literature Review

pmc-13077662.description: Background and AimsNeurodegenerative disorders are marked by progressive deterioration of neurons, affecting cognitive, memory, and motor functions. This decline creates substantial personal and social challenges, making early identification of risk factors essential for effective intervention. Environmental toxicants, such as chemicals and air pollutants, are suspected to negatively impact brain health.
